newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors begin roll into Julys.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors begin roll into Julys.

text.p: The monthly moving of positions from the front month out to longer-dated months picked up steam Wednesday ahead of next week's expiration of June options, traders said.

"We're getting people rolling short calls into next month," the head of one options trading desk said. "We're trying to get all our brokers doing stuff this week instead of waiting until the last minute."
Another options trader also said investors were beginning to move out of their June positions, which expire at the end of next week.
Overall, traders said equity options activity was relatively quiet.
"I think we're just waiting for the bond market to make a move one way or the other," the trading desk chief said.
Office Depot Inc options, traded on the American Stock Exchange, continued to attract the most business, with activity in the July series again leading the trade.
The Office Depot July 17-1/2 calls traded more than 6,600 contracts by 1145 CDT/1645 GMT and the July 20 calls traded about 6,565.
The July 15 puts traded 6,240 and the July 12-1/2 puts traded 5,840.
Office Depot shares were unchanged at 17-3/4 on consolidated volume of about 1.05 million shares.

Investors are waiting to see whether a U.S. District Court judge sides with the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, which is seeking to block Office Depot's planned merger with Staples Inc, or with the two office superstores.
After a five-day hearing in late May, Judge Thomas Hogan said he would rule by mid-June.
Staples options, which trade on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, were fairly quiet, with only the July 20 calls seeing much action.
Turnover in those calls was 1,400 contracts.
Staples was down 1/16 at 22-15/16 on roughly 837,000 shares.
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange, a sizable spread crossed in Bay Networks Inc options, traders said.
The Bay Networks July 22-1/2 call traded about 6,745 contracts and the June 17-1/2 call traded 3,245.
"One firm crossed the spread. A customer was a seller of the spread so they bought the July 22-1/2s and sold the June 17-1/2s," said a market maker.

He said the spread was done on a two-to-one basis and that some of it could be rolling out from June to July. But he said it was difficult to determine as yet how much of it was opening positions and how much was closing.
Bay Networks shares were up 1/4 at 22. Turnover topped 1.4 million shares.
